topic: Arc length to central angle in degrees
problem: A circle has a radius of 12 centimeters. An arc of the circle has a length of 10pi centimeters. What is the measure, in degrees, of the central angle that intercepts this arc?

bad.why: On paper the student must solve the proportion x/360 = 10pi/(24pi) for x by cross-multiplying, or use s = r*theta (not on the reference sheet) and convert 5pi/6 radians to degrees: hand rearrangement the graph replaces.
Typed into Desmos, the same computation still needs s = r*theta and the 180/pi conversion (neither on the reference sheet), or the proportion solved for x by hand; the graph needs neither.

algebraFirst.description: Sets 10pi = (theta/360)(2pi)(12) and solves theta = 360(10pi)/(24pi) = 150, or uses s = r*theta to get 5pi/6 radians and converts with 180/pi.

explanationNotes: An arc is a fraction of the whole circumference: a central angle of x degrees out of 360 gives an arc of length (x/360)(2pi)(12). Graph that next to y = 10pi and click where they meet, (150, 31.42), so x = 150 degrees with no equation solved by hand and no radian conversion. Zoom out on the x-axis, since the crossing is far to the right.
